title: Interview with Pastor Doug Leaman
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: Early Life and Conversion
subpoints: Born in Brazil to a pastor father
Grew up in a Christian home with early gospel exposure
Describes conversion as a 'blessed innocence' and gradual realization of God's importance

outline.title: Struggle with Fear of Man
subpoints: Identified social anxiety and shyness as spiritual issues
Influenced by Wayne Mack’s work on the fear of man
Recognized connection between pride, anxiety, and seeking human approval

outline.title: Call to Ministry and Biblical Counseling
subpoints: Discovered biblical counseling at Masters College
Recognized a gap in Reformed Presbyterian theology regarding internal struggles
Found value in addressing soul-level issues through the gospel rather than solely medical means

outline.title: Missionary Work in Brazil
subpoints: Aimed to introduce biblical counseling to Brazilian churches
Navigated cultural and logistical challenges in the mission field

summary:
In this afternoon interview, Pastor Tito Lyro speaks with Pastor Doug Leaman about his life, faith, and ministry. Pastor Leaman shares his testimony of growing up in a Christian home in Brazil, where he was born to a pastor father. He describes his early spiritual journey as one of 'blessed innocence,' noting that the Holy Spirit transformed his heart from a young age, leading to a deep understanding of God's sovereignty and his own identity as a child of God.

A significant portion of the conversation addresses Pastor Leaman's personal struggle with the 'fear of man,' social anxiety, and pride. He explains how he came to view these issues through a biblical lens, influenced by the work of Wayne Mack and the discipline of biblical counseling. This theological perspective allowed him to understand that his desire for human approval and his anxiety were rooted in idolatry, which the gospel addresses at the level of the soul and heart.

Pastor Leaman also discusses his call to ministry, which was solidified during his studies at Masters College. He recognized a significant gap in the Reformed Presbyterian community regarding the application of biblical counseling to internal struggles. This realization, combined with his own healing, drove him to pursue ministry in Brazil, where he has worked to introduce and promote biblical counseling among local churches, addressing both spiritual and psychological needs through the power of the gospel.
